site.frontage: A360 High Street, to the south-west
site.note: Lat/lon derived from the MAGiC grid reference via OSGB36->WGS84 Helmert transform. Accurate to ~1m; good enough for a true sun path.
site.orientationNote: The building run goes SW -> NE: the commercial building at 79a sits at the SW end nearest the A360, then the house, then the double garage at the NE end. So on the agent plan, left is SW and right is NE, which puts plan-up at a bearing of 315 (north-west). Confirmed against the MAGiC extract, the title plan and the architect elevation names.

provenance.floorPlan: Estate agent plan, 'Total Area: 135.4 m2 / 1458 ft2'
provenance.titlePlan: HM Land Registry style plot extract
provenance.records: Council tax band D; last sold 267500 GBP on 2007-04-19
provenance.architectDrawing: Waters Architects, 'Existing plan & elevs 1/50 & 1/100 @ A3' — NW, SE and SW elevations plus an existing 1:50 floor plan of the attached single-storey structure
provenance.interiors: Marketing interior photographs (19 in set): living room, kitchen, dining room, bedroom
provenance.revision: Rebuilt 2026-08-25 (4th pass). Every wall, room and opening is now measured off the estate agent plan by pixel analysis at 81.04 px/m, not estimated by eye. The building is 7.26m deep, not the 8.41m previously forced; the invented rear hall is gone.
provenance.method: PIL threshold at luminance<100, wall bands found by column/row ink density, each band's extent recovered as contiguous runs. Scale fixed from the dining room's labelled 3.64m.

construction.walls: red brick, exposed on the flank and rear; the south-west front is largely covered by Virginia creeper
construction.periodEvidence: Hipped roof, picture rails and deep coving, tall ground-floor ceilings, cast-iron bedroom fireplaces, brick chimney breasts to both floors.
construction.wallThicknessNote: Inter-war brick could be solid 9-inch (230mm) or early cavity (270-300mm). Still using 300mm. An EPC or a reveal measurement at any window settles it.

climb.note: Walking into this footprint carries you up; stepping off the top puts you on the landing. It stops short of the bathroom doorway at y=3.94 so that heading for the toilet does not send you upstairs.

roofs.note: Continues the hip over the full-depth west column; its front edge runs into the main roof.
Lean-to over the bathroom and shower. Measured rear extent 5.59m — forward of the garage at 6.02m and well forward of the kitchen wing at 7.26m.

Hipped at the free north-east end and along both long sides, closing as a gable where it meets the house. The near-square footprint made a plain hip collapse into a pyramid, which is not what the aerial shows.
Small pitched canopy over the front door, hipped on its three free sides and closing against the wall — as the aerial shows.

chimneys.note: Brick stack carried up off its breast and emerging near the ridge. Plan size and height above the roof are set so it reads as domestic brickwork, not a tower.

features.note: Detected on the plan in the living room east wall — stone surround, wood-burning stove.
Brick fireplace with timber mantel and alcove shelving, on the wall through to the kitchen.

structures.name: 79a — front part
structures.note: The larger part, nearest the road. The architect's south-east elevation shows its gable end with vertical boarding above a window.

structures.name: 79a — back part
structures.note: The part further back, running alongside the house and abutting it at the kitchen end. Owner-confirmed mono-pitch sloping up against the house wall — this is the architect's north-west elevation. It sits back 1.3m from the gabled part, which projects further towards the road — owner-verified against the street photographs.

assumptions.title: The shower room door is invented
assumptions.detail: No door gap was detectable on the plan for the shower room. One is placed so the room is reachable at all. Everything else on this floor comes from a measured gap in a wall.

assumptions.title: No door drawn between the house and the garage
assumptions.detail: The garage is attached and shares the house east wall, but the plan shows no internal connecting door — the only garage door besides the two up-and-over doors is a personnel door in its back wall. Unusual for an attached double garage, so worth confirming.

assumptions.title: Ceiling heights inferred from photographs
assumptions.detail: 2.65m ground, 2.35m kitchen, 2.30m under the lean-to, 2.45m first floor, read from picture-rail and coving proportions. A tape measure on any one wall corrects all of them.

assumptions.title: Wall construction not confirmed
assumptions.detail: The plan draws external walls at 230mm and internal at 170mm, which is now what the model uses — consistent with solid 9-inch brick. An EPC would confirm.

assumptions.title: Roof pitches and eaves are assumed
assumptions.detail: Hips at 38 degrees, garage 35, lean-to 15. Footprints are measured; the third dimension is not.

assumptions.title: Net area runs 5% under the plan total
assumptions.detail: Modelled room areas sum to 128.7m2 against the plan's stated 135.4m2. Room rectangles here are internal while the plan total is gross external, and 5% is the expected gap for a house with this much wall.

assumptions.title: Orientation derived, not given
assumptions.detail: The building run reads SW to NE off the MAGiC and title extracts, putting plan-up at bearing 315. Geometry is unaffected; a sun path would not be.

assumptions.title: Stair geometry standard, not surveyed
assumptions.detail: 14 risers at 211mm with a 215mm going, fitted to the measured hall.

assumptions.title: A panelled structure abuts the rear flank
assumptions.detail: The rear photograph shows a large white panelled wall with failing paint. If that is asbestos cement it matters well beyond this model.

assumptions.title: How far 79a comes forward is a judgement
assumptions.detail: Modelled projecting 5.0m past the front of the house, per the owner note to move it forward and the title plan showing it reaching past the south-west corner. The exact overhang is not measurable from any sheet supplied.

assumptions.title: Chimney stack positions inferred from breasts
assumptions.detail: Placed over the dining and living-room chimney breasts — the living-room one is detected on the plan, the dining one is from the photographs. The aerial shows two stacks in roughly these places, but neither is measured.

assumptions.title: Plot dimensions +/-8%
assumptions.detail: Traced from the title-plan crop and scaled off the building. 374m2, about a tenth of an acre, with 9.3m of front garden and 4.7m beside the garage.

assumptions.title: The landing alcove is closed off by inference
assumptions.detail: The plan shows no wall along the alcove's south side, which would leave the two west bedrooms running into each other. One is added so each bedroom has a single door, which is what the owner confirms. Worth checking on site.

plot.source: Fitted to the HM Land Registry title plan by optimising overlap between the model's own ground footprint and the building tint on the plan. Best fit: rotation 318.72 deg, scale 38.32 px/m, IoU 0.862.

validation.polygonVsMask: traced polygon 379m2 against a 381m2 mask, 0.5% apart
validation.independentCheck: 79a's footprint falls out of the same transform at x -4.6..0.0, y -5.0..5.3, against -4.60..0 and -4.45..5.65 derived separately from the architect's 1:50 plan. Two unrelated sources agreeing to ~0.4m.
validation.method: tools/verify-plot-fit.py regenerates the overlay so the fit can be re-checked by eye.

commercialBuildingSurvey.scaleAnchor: A 1.5m window opening in the back wall gives 87.3 px/m, so 11.3 x 5.1m overall, split 7.2m and 4.1m. That is the only reading consistent with the title plan, the aerial and the building being comparable in size to the house.
commercialBuildingSurvey.unresolved: The elevations on the same sheet imply roughly half that scale, which would make the building about 21m long. That contradicts every other source, so the plan-based reading is used. Two real dimensions would settle it in seconds.
commercialBuildingSurvey.elevationReading: The south-west elevation shows the house behind: hip slopes rising to a ridge with a chimney above, and 79a attached to its right as a lower single-storey range with a long horizontal roofline.

measuredOnMap.footprint: 10.1 x 4.6m, area 36m2, long axis 89.2 degrees to the house — i.e. perpendicular, running parallel to the road exactly as described.
measuredOnMap.resolvesScale: This supersedes the assumed 1.5m window. The real opening works out at about 1.34m, so the plan-based reading was close and the elevation-based one (21m) is wrong.

commercialBuildingSurvey.planningRef: Mathewson Waters Architects, MWA 19110 (2020), applicant Mrs Lynn Rooke
commercialBuildingSurvey.confirmed: A single-storey 1930s building, attached to but NOT part of No. 79. Formerly retail and hairdressing, vacant for some years. The 2020 application sought consent to replace it with a single-storey office and archive for a farming business.
commercialBuildingSurvey.siting: On the corner of the A360 and Russell Mill Lane. Photographs show a half-timbered gable end facing the corner and a long rendered elevation with shopfront windows to the road, under a tiled multi-pitch roof.
commercialBuildingSurvey.boundaryResolved: The title boundary runs between the two buildings: 79a abuts No. 79 across it. That is why 79a is modelled touching the house yet lying outside the parcel.
